{"self_assessment": "Impact: I kept the table supplied so the builders never had to stop. I made three batch trips to the boxes, 40 dominoes each, into the shared bin (at about 0:45, 1:45 and 3:00). Big batches are far cheaper per domino than small ones, and the bin stayed stocked throughout, so nobody left the table to fetch. The fish was fully connected from the start, with all 113 standing dominoes in the run, and I contributed to that by keeping materials available.

Execution: I stuck to my supply role and did it reliably. I fetched in large batches, kept an eye on the bin level and reported it to the table (52 at one point), and timed the next trip so it never ran thin. After the third trip the bin was well stocked, so I stopped fetching rather than carrying more than was needed. I stayed hands-off the build once it was connected, so nothing got bumped before the push.

Collaboration: I communicated clearly and often about bin status, so the builders knew when to ask and when not to worry. I supported Jack's fish plan from the start, took on the supply job so the others could concentrate on building, and encouraged everyone to keep hands off near the end.

Leadership: I took ownership of a necessary function without being asked twice, and I made the role visible by announcing what I was doing and when. I backed the group's decision quickly instead of reopening it, which helped us move fast. I also kept the table focused on the finish by calling for hands off before the push.

I don't know how the judge scored the picture, but the fish was fully connected, and reliable supply was a real part of that. Other builders did the laying, which was the larger part of the work. I'd put my share at about 25 percent.", "my_share_percent": 25}
